detail: Offline unit. Objective: find why one request's response is written twice, add request_sha256 + row_seq to every row, prove the identity discriminates, propose the ledger rule. Bound 28 calls. No inference, no network.

One resp object consumed by two make_row calls, not a retry/resume/second writer. run_longrun.py:2105-2109 rebinds `resp` to fetch_rounds()' return (the LAST follow-up's response, built at run_longrun.py:964-965 and turned into a kind=tool-followup row at 973-978); run_longrun.py:2167 then builds the kind=turn row from that same object. Both appended: 2177-2178 (follow-up) then 2179 (turn). Condition: tools_enabled(cfg) and not is_answer_turn and at least one follow-up round bought; with zero follow-ups fetch_rounds returns the passed-in resp so no duplicate. The turn's own initial send (run_longrun.py:2045, counted at 2050) gets no row of its own. Confirmed on the three quoted pairs: identical ts/ttft_s/latency_s/content_sha256/tokens, different prompt_sha256.

client.send_chat now hashes the exact wire bytes (request_sha256, request_identity_complete; wall-cap rows stamped via TurnWallCap.fields). make_row writes both fields on every row (unknown/false when the body was not retained). append_row assigns a monotonic per-file row_seq once per row object. Test 17/17 green, and red when the field is stripped (KeyError request_sha256). Historical backfill: 0 of 1,101 rows in 14 files retain any part of the request body. Rows files untouched.

Find the double append behind the 30 dropped rows and make it visible: add request_sha256 (sha256 of the exact wire body) + request_identity_complete + row_seq to every row, prove the identity separates one-send-written-twice from two-sends-same-text, and state the rule the ledger should adopt without editing it. OFFLINE, zero inference requests, 28-call bound.

Read measure/DUPLICATE-ATTACK.md (V-DUPLICATE-RULE: content_sha256 = sha256(assistant content), 869/869 at run_longrun.py:1555; 30/30 dropped rows identical to 6dp on ttft_s/latency_s) and walked the writer: run_longrun.py:2045 initial send -> :2082 counted -> :2092 tool path -> :964 follow-up send -> :974 follow-up row built from that resp -> :980 the same resp returned -> :2106 rebound -> :2152 initial prompt hash -> :2167 turn row built from the same resp -> :2178-2179 both rows written. No retry loop in client.py (RequestFailure raises, the runner stops at :2076-2083); --resume replays through planner.replay (:1904) without re-appending.

Independent re-derivation, experiments/ptr-engine/tools/dedupe_root_cause.py (own loader, own tuple, no import of the author's helper): 1101 rows / 14 files / 30 hash-applicable groups / 30 excess; 41 groups / 54 excess counting the three legacy files' naive same-second tuple; 30/30 decided pairs identical on every measured field; only kind pair observed tool-followup/turn. Walked pairs: v4-tools T1 (2 rows, 2 sends, 1 measurement), v5-tools T2 (3 rows, 3 sends, 2 measurements), v6 T1 (2 rows, 2 sends, 1 measurement) — one send per turn stands without a measurement of its own.

DOUBLE APPEND FOUND, at run_longrun.py:974 (kind=tool-followup row built from resp) and run_longrun.py:2167 (kind=turn row built from the SAME resp returned at :980 and rebound at :2106). Condition: tools_enabled(cfg) and not is_answer_turn AND at least one follow-up request granted. Not a retry and not an extra row: N+1 sends vs N+1 rows with N distinct measurements, so the turn row wears the follow-up's numbers while hashing the initial prompt (:2152) — a misattribution. Deducting the 30 would understate spend by 30.

docs/REQUEST-IDENTITY.md written: field contract (request_sha256 at client.py:656-660, request_identity_complete, row_seq at run_longrun.py:1686-1700 seeded from the file high-water mark), the file:line walk, the 3 walked pairs, the recommended rule, and the honest zero for history.

python3 experiments/ptr-engine/longrun/tests/test_request_identity.py -> 17 checks, 0 failed, exit 0 (case a: different requests differ on request_sha256 while content_sha256 collides; b: re-send same hash, row_seq 1->2; c: one send two rows same hash and same row_seq; d: the historical pair rebuilt with the real make_row). Zero network: socket.socket replaced by a raise for the run.

python3 .../test_request_identity.py --red-green -> 'RED with the guards reverted: new identity keeps them apart on the row itself, same object written twice -> same row_seq, duplicate = same request_sha256 AND same row_seq' then 'RED->GREEN: 3 check(s) red with the identity reverted, all green restored'. Reversion happens in memory (make_row writes the old response hash; append_row re-sequences every write); nothing on disk is modified to make the test fail.

Backfill question: 0 of 1101 rows can be given a true request identity — no row retained the body (request_sha256 0, request_identity_complete 0, row_seq 0, request body 0). The serialized body lives only as a local in send_chat and dies with the process, so a hash computed now would be a guess. Rows files untouched: every measure/rows-*.jsonl keeps its pre-session mtime.

Suite neighbours: python3 -m unittest discover -s experiments/ptr-engine/longrun/tests -p 'test_*.py' -> 118 tests, 2 failures, both test_decidability_seam ('grader decidable=3' vs decidable=1). Not in this unit's change surface: that test writes its own rows.jsonl (tests/test_decidability_seam.py:103) and never imports the runner's writer; the disagreement is grade_v5.py:653 vs analyze_stats.py:457. Recorded, not hidden.

Done. Double append located at run_longrun.py:974 + :2167 with its condition; rows now carry request_sha256 / request_identity_complete / row_seq; the three-way discriminator passes (17/17) and goes red when reverted (3/3); 0 historical rows are backfillable and history is byte-identical; the ledger rule recommendation is stated in docs/REQUEST-IDENTITY.md §4 for the ledger's owner.
